items.statement: Physical assignment of the 1a lower-energy absorption band
items.expected: For full neutral singlet 1a, actual state-resolved excitation and orbital or transition-density evidence assigns the lower-energy absorption feature to a singlet pi–pi* excitation, with source-compatible dominant HOMO-to-LUMO character or a demonstrated physically equivalent state description. Report the calculated energy/wavelength and intensity under a stated molecular environment, and distinguish them from the supplied toluene band maximum. A frontier gap, copied band maximum, or nearest-root choice without physical character does not establish the assignment. This outcome scores the physical identity of the band, not a separate optimization, frequency or orbital-generation step.

items.statement: Electronic explanation of the shifts across 1a–1d
items.expected: Actual comparable excitation and state/orbital evidence connects the lower transition energies of each of 1b, 1c and 1d relative to 1a to extension and connectivity of the aromatic pi system. The added final finding is the molecular electronic explanation, not repetition of the supplied experimental red shifts. Distinct fused connectivities need not have identical excited states, and no robust ordering between 1c and 1d or universal causal decomposition is required. Explain the declared molecular medium and the limits of comparing vertical roots with toluene absorption maxima. Source and calculated wavelengths are contextual; no hard nm window is defined.

items.statement: Physical explanation of the weak lower-energy 1c band
items.expected: Actual comparable transition strengths and state-character evidence explain the low intensity of the lower-energy 1c feature relative to the corresponding 1b and 1d bands: its lowest pi–pi* transition carries much less oscillator strength. The explanation must follow calculated transition intensity rather than observed extinction coefficients, an orbital gap, or a list of state labels. The source f values 0.008/0.143/0.135 are non-scoring context, not hard windows. This outcome concerns the intensity contrast; the physical identity of the 1c low state is scored separately.

items.statement: Physical assignment of the stronger higher-energy 1c band
items.expected: Actual energy, transition-strength and state-character evidence attributes the stronger higher-energy 1c absorption feature to higher singlet pi–pi* contributions rather than identifying the brightest band with the lowest state. The source representation involves HOMO to LUMO+1 and HOMO-1 to LUMO contributions (S2/S3), but these are supporting state descriptions, not independently required computational nodes or fixed root indices. A physically equivalent mixed-state or spectral account passes when it establishes the higher-band origin and relative brightness. Distinguish the observed 339 nm maximum from calculated vertical roots; no exact line-shape fit or source wavelength window is required.
